label: linux-chrome-idle

machine.description: 4 vCPU x86_64 container (gVisor), Debian 12 (bookworm), 32 GB RAM, no GPU
machine.quiet_check: top -bn1 before each web run and before tooling: no cargo/rustc/gradle/other chrome; only idle background processes (two `axiom run` fixture servers of unit c at ~6% CPU of one core each, a python http.server). Gradle daemons were stopped after the APK builds and before the web runs.

notes: Web numbers: headless Chrome on a 4 vCPU Linux container (no GPU), release build (dart2js), server on 127.0.0.1. Not a physical device.
All three clients call the same local Dart server (api/server); see README for method.

Box was idle (checked with top before every run; see machine.quiet_check). Run 1 was made right after the release build; its small-call medians are 0.1-0.3 ms higher for all three clients, which is what pushes those ~2 ms metrics over the 10% spread.
axiom pull used the released CLI 0.156.0 with the branch generator resolved through the app's path dependency (the CLI does not read AXIOM_FLUTTER_SDK_PATH).
The bench drops the Axiom query key after every call (AxiomQueryManager().remove) so each call is a network request; this is the same workload as for dio/http.

web_stats.rule: median of 3 run medians; publishable if (max-min)/median <= 10%

runtime.wasm_runtime_commit: axiom-runtime 1265a1c (flutter/h: host notify + WS send fixes)

generator_path_used_by_axiom_pull: Released CLI 0.156.0 does not read AXIOM_FLUTTER_SDK_PATH (the string is not in the binary; axiom-build/src/core/utils.rs runs `dart run axiom_flutter_generator:generate` in the app). That resolves through app/pubspec.yaml, whose dev_dependency is a path dependency on ../../axiom_flutter_generator, so `axiom pull` ran the branch generator (not the published one).

tooling.method:
Client generation time: `axiom pull` end to end and the Axiom generator alone vs
`dart run build_runner build` for the retrofit/json_serializable client. 5 runs each, cold and warm.

  python3 tool/bench_tooling.py [--runs 5] [--out results/tooling.json]

cold  = tool caches removed first: the generator's compiled snapshot
        (app/.dart_tool/pub/bin/axiom_flutter_generator) for Axiom, `build_runner clean`
        (compiled build script + asset graph) for build_runner. pub's package cache stays warm.
warm  = caches present. Axiom always regenerates every file (no incremental mode). For
        build_runner a comment in api.dart and models.dart is changed before every warm run so
        it has to regenerate both .g.dart files (an unchanged warm run is a no-op and is
        reported separately as warm_noop).
Discarded caches are moved to build/trash (never deleted).

loc.method:
Lines of code per client approach. Counts non-blank lines that are not only a comment
(`//`, `///`, `#`). Prints JSON; `--out FILE` writes it.

Hand-written files per approach are listed in FILES below; generated files are counted
separately and never added to the hand-written total. For Acore the contract also carries the
server implementation (`managed { ... }` bodies); those lines are reported separately
(`acore_managed_bodies`) so a reader can compare declarations only. The contract also declares a
WebSocket endpoint the other clients do not have: `hand_written_unary_only` subtracts it.

size.method:
App size with and without the Axiom SDK.

  python3 tool/bench_size.py [--out results/size.json] [--skip-apk] [--skip-web]

baseline = baseline_app/lib/main.dart (dio + http, one call each, no axiom_flutter dependency)
axiom    = app/lib/size_main.dart (the same screen plus one Axiom call; app depends on axiom_flutter)
Builds: `flutter build apk --release --split-per-abi` and `flutter build web --release`.
Web sizes: main.dart.js, every file under build/web, the Axiom wasm/js assets, and gzip -9
sizes of the largest files (what a server with gzip would transfer).
